title: Jensen bound for the sampled payoff against a pure column
statement:
Let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ take values in $[0,1]$, and let $x : [M] \to \bbr$ and $y : [N] \to \bbr$ be finite families of row and column points, giving rise to the sampled game whose $(i,j)$ entry is $f(x_i, y_j)$. Fix a column index $j$, and suppose the section $x' \mapsto f(x', y_j)$ is convex on a set $X \subseteq \bbr$ with $x_i \in X$ for every $i$. Then for any mixed row strategy $p$ over the $M$ rows,
\[
  f\!\left(\sum_{i} p_i\, x_i,\; y_j\right) \;\le\; \sum_{i} p_i\, f(x_i, y_j),
\]
where the right-hand side is the expected payoff of the sampled game against column $j$ under $p$.
hypotheses_covered: f takes values in [0,1] (payoff nonnegative and at most one)
finite row points x and column points y
p is a mixed strategy over the M rows
replaced:
If $f(\cdot, y_j)$ is convex on $X$ and every $x_i \in X$, then for any mixed
row strategy $p \in \Delta_M$,
\[
  f\!\left(\sum_i p_i\,x_i,\; y_j\right)
  \;\leq\;
  \mathrm{payoffVsPure}(\mathrm{sampledGame},\,p,\,j).
\]
That is, convexity in the row variable means the continuous mixed-action payoff
is at most the finite-game expected payoff.
